summary: Georgios T. Halkias is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and became the Glorious Sun Endowed Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong in 2025.

Gerald B. Kelley was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. After earning his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he served there as an assistant professor from ~1959 to 1963 before becoming a professor at Cornell University in 1963.

Gerald Hüther studied at the University of Leipzig from ~1969 to 1974. He worked at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine (1979–1989) and held posts at the University of Göttingen and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen (~1995–2016).

Gerald James Larson specialized in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, earning his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He was a professor of religious studies at UC Santa Barbara from 1972 and Rabindranath Tagore Professor Emeritus at Indiana University Bloomington in 1995.

Gerald Patrick Moriarty was a historian and Indologist who studied at Balliol College, Oxford, and Pembroke College. He worked in the Indian Civil Service, tutored at Oxford around 1889, and served as University Teacher of Indian History at Cambridge (1897–1924).

Gerald Schwedler is a historian who studied at Heidelberg University. He served as a research assistant at the University of Zurich (2015–2018), substitute professor at Konstanz and Heidelberg, and took up a post at Kiel University in 2018.

Gerard Abraham Joseph worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He was appointed Secretary and Librarian at the National Museum of Colombo in 1893 and served as a member of the Ceylon Civil Service from ~1902 to 1922.

Gerard Leslie Makins Clauson worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Eton College and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1910–1914), he later held a post at the University of Oxford.
Gerardus van der Leeuw was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. After studying at Leiden University from ~1908 to 1916, he held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.

Gerasim Stepanovich Lebedev was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Golok Nath Das in 1787. In 1801, he became an interpreter at the Collegium of Foreign Affairs and served in the Département asiatique from ~1801 to 1817.
Gerd J. R. Mevissen is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin, attested in 2017 and as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter in 2026.
Gerda Hartmann was an Indologist who earned her Ph.D. at Kiel University (~1927–1932) studying under Friedrich Otto Schrader. She later worked at the Library of Congress from 1938 to 1940.

Gereon Kopf is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his degree at Temple University. He taught at Luther College (attested 2001–2015) and conducted research at J. F. Oberlin and Nanzan Universities.

Gergana Ruseva is an Indologist who earned an MA at Sofia University. She worked as a physicist at the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences (2000–2009) and served as a lecturer (2000) and associate professor (2012) at Sofia University.

Gergely Hidas is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He was a Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014) and a postdoctoral researcher at the British Museum (2014).

Gergely Orosz is a Tibetology scholar who earned a PhD at Budapest University of Technology and Economics (2018–2023), becoming an assistant professor there in 2023. He also worked as a librarian at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (attested 2002).

Gerhard Czerny was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the universities of Vienna, Rostock, and Erlangen-Nuremberg between 1923 and 1927, studying under Julius von Negelein and Paul Althaus.
Gerhard Meiser was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the universities of Munich, Belgrade, Sarajevo, Regensburg, and Freiburg between ~1972 and 1985.

Gerhard Oberhammer was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Innsbruck and studied under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan. He held posts at Utrecht University (1961) and the University of Vienna (1964–1997).

Gerhard Wolf is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Heidelberg University (~1972–1989). He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1995–1998), Trier University (~1998–2003), and the Max Planck Society (~2003–2020).
